newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle close up ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle close up ahead of report.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher on mixed support ahead of the USDA semi-annual U.S. Cattle Inventory report, traders said.

Live cattle finished 0.500 to 0.100 cent higher with February up 0.350 at 64.750 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.400 to 0.100 with March up 0.275 at 69.675 cents. May posted a new contract high of 71.000 cents.

Most trading represented evening up of positions ahead of the report to be released Friday afternoon. Expectations the report will show lower U.S. cattle numbers kept futures prices higher, they said.

Analyst projections on the inventory report averaged 98.1 percent of last year, or 101.83 million head, for total U.S. cattle numbers on January 1. Actual numbers ranged from 100.9 to 103.8 million head, 97 to 100.2 percent of last year. All categories are seen showing declines from last year.

An upturn in cash beef prices also lent support to nearby live cattle futures. Choice boxed beef recently set their lowest price level since May 6 and prices are likely firming on increased retailer interest. Boxed sales have been active the past few days and expectations are that retailers will be featuring beef, they added.
In live cattle options, funds were buying June 64 calls and selling August futures. Commission houses executed the February 64 straddle. Trading was light ahead of the report, pit sources said.
Feeders also rose on the projections for reduced cattle numbers in the inventory report. The report is expected to show tighter feeder supplies this year, traders said.

Added support was also coming from concern over death losses this winter and expected calving problems this spring due to the storms and bitter cold. USDA was already citing possible calving problems from lack of feed, they said.

Deputy Secretary of Agriculture Richard Rominger said the severe weather recently has caused nutritional problems for cattle, and predicted that many cows will be too weak by spring to have their calves, or that many calves will be too weak to survive.
Lower corn futures also lent support, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.04 at $69.60 per cwt.
